item.title: Shaping Africa’s Digital Future Through Cybersecurity and AI
item.dc:creator: James Momanyi
item.description: TVETA is proud to participate in the 5th Edition of Cyberweek Africa 2026, taking place at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) from 27th–30th October 2026 under the theme: “Cyber Threat Intelligence in the Age of AI.” The conference was officially opened by Principal Secretary for Broadcasting and Telecommunications, Mr. Stephen Isaboke, EBS, bringing together [...]
item.content:encoded:
TVETA is proud to participate in the 5th Edition of Cyberweek Africa 2026, taking place at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) from 27th–30th October 2026 under the theme: “Cyber Threat Intelligence in the Age of AI.”

The conference was officially opened by Principal Secretary for Broadcasting and Telecommunications, Mr. Stephen Isaboke, EBS, bringing together policymakers, industry leaders, innovators, and cybersecurity experts to explore how Africa can harness emerging technologies while strengthening digital resilience.

Key reflections from the opening sessions remind us that:

Despite advances in technology, human ingenuity, critical thinking, and ethical

leadership must remain at the centre of innovation.

As the world develops the rules that govern AI, Africa must actively shape and contribute to that future.

The continent’s greatest strength lies in leveraging technology to amplify Africa’s talent, innovation, and opportunities.

As the regulator of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Kenya, TVETA remains committed to assuring quality and relevance in TVET training, fostering skills development that responds to emerging technologies and industry needs, and promoting programmes that prepare learners for the digital economy. Through strengthened digital, technical, and innovation skills, TVETA continues to support the development of a competent workforce capable of driving Kenya’s cybersecurity readiness and Africa’s digital transformation.

item.title: TVETA Strengthens Quality Assurance Capacity at Wote Technical and Vocational Training College
item.dc:creator: James Momanyi
item.description: The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) is conducting a one-week capacity-building workshop on the Kenya National TVET Quality Assurance Framework and Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) System for trainers at Wote Technical and Vocational Training College. The training aims to strengthen participants’ understanding and practical application of quality assurance principles, processes and standards [...]
item.content:encoded:
The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) is conducting a one-week capacity-building workshop on the Kenya National TVET Quality Assurance Framework and Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) System for trainers at Wote Technical and Vocational Training College.

The training aims to strengthen participants’ understanding and practical application of quality assurance principles, processes and standards to enhance the quality and relevance of training delivery.

Key areas covered include the rationale and benefits of TVET quality assurance; the quality assurance cycle and ability model; the Input-Process-Output (IPO) model; quality assurance framework enablers and elements; and the Quality Standards Indicators for TVET Providers.

Participants are also being equipped with practical skills in Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET) curriculum support, development and review of IQA policies, preparation for quality evaluation, audit planning, institutional quality evaluation and analysis of audit findings.

The workshop also addresses developing IQA action and work plans, quality assurance for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), and strategies to overcome barriers to effective implementation of internal quality assurance systems.

Through practical exercises and simulated institutional evaluations, the trainers are gaining insights into identifying quality gaps, documenting findings and developing corrective actions to support continuous improvement.

The workshop is part of a series of capacity-building initiatives planned by TVETA for the current financial year to strengthen quality assurance across TVET institutions.

TVETA remains committed to building institutional capacity, promoting a culture of continuous improvement and ensuring that trainees receive quality, relevant and industry-responsive skills training.

item.dc:creator: James Momanyi

Dr Wanyeki brings over 15 years of experience in TVET regulation, policy development, quality assurance, institutional leadership and skills development. He [...]
item.content:encoded:
The Board of Directors of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr Paul Machocho Wanyeki as the Director General/Chief Executive Officer of the Authority.

Dr Wanyeki brings over 15 years of experience in TVET regulation, policy development, quality assurance, institutional leadership and skills development. He has held senior leadership positions at TVETA, including Acting Director of Standards Development, Compliance and Enforcement, where he contributed to strengthening regulatory and quality assurance systems and advancing key national TVET reforms. He previously served at Dedan Kimathi University of Technology and as a trainer at Kisiwa National Polytechnic.

Congratulating Dr Wanyeki on his appointment, TVETA Board Chairperson, Prof. Kellen Kiambati, expressed confidence in his leadership and ability to advance the Authority’s strategic priorities. She noted that his extensive experience and deep understanding of the TVET sector would be instrumental in strengthening the quality, relevance and credibility of Kenya’s TVET system.

The Board also recognized and commended Mr Timothy Nyongesa Katiambo for his dedicated service and leadership during his tenure as Acting Director General.

The Board congratulates Dr Wanyeki on his appointment and wishes him success as he leads TVETA’s Management and staff in fulfilling the Authority’s mandate and supporting the Government’s skills development and economic transformation agenda.

item.title: TVETA Hands Over Accreditation Certificate to Kenya Coast National Polytechnic, Kwale Campus
item.dc:creator: James Momanyi
item.description: On Friday, the Acting Director General of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA), Timothy Nyongesa Katiambo, on Friday joined the Principal Secretary for Technical and Vocational Education and Training, Dr Esther Thaara Muoria, and the World Bank EASTRIP Implementation Support Mission for a site visit to the Kenya Coast National Polytechnic Centre [...]
item.content:encoded:
On Friday, the Acting Director General of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA), Timothy Nyongesa Katiambo, on Friday joined the Principal Secretary for Technical and Vocational Education and Training, Dr Esther Thaara Muoria, and the World Bank EASTRIP Implementation Support Mission for a site visit to the Kenya Coast National Polytechnic Centre of Excellence in Maritime and Port Logistics in Waa, Kwale County.

During the visit, the Acting Director General formally handed over the TVETA accreditation certificate to the newly registered Kenya Coast National Polytechnic, Kwale Campus, marking an important milestone in the institution’s establishment and its readiness to offer approved training programmes.

The visit formed part of the one-week closing mission for the East Africa Skills for Transformation and Regional Integration Project (EASTRIP), which brought together the World Bank Group, the State Department for TVET through the National Project Coordinating Unit, representatives of Kenya’s five Regional Flagship TVET Institutions, TVETA and other partner agencies.

The mission reviewed project implementation progress assessed achievements and identified priority actions ahead of the project’s scheduled closure on 31 December 2026.

Earlier, the mission conducted site visits to Kisumu National Polytechnic, KenGen Geothermal Training Centre, the Kenya Institute of Highways and Building Technology (KIHBT), and Meru National Polytechnic to assess progress and achievements at the respective Regional Flagship TVET Institutions.

The EASTRIP initiative has played a significant role in strengthening specialised TVET training infrastructure and capacity, with a focus on developing industry-responsive skills that support regional integration, productivity and economic transformation.

TVETA remains committed to ensuring that institutions meet the required regulatory and quality standards, safeguarding the integrity and credibility of training while expanding access to relevant, high-quality technical and vocational skills.

item.description: The EASTRIP SDTVET/World Bank Mission has commenced its closing implementation support mission and National Steering Committee (NSC) meetings with a site visit to Kisumu National Polytechnic, home to the KSh 1.2 billion World Bank-funded East Africa Skills for Transformation and Regional Integration Project (EASTRIP). Designated as the Regional Flagship TVET Institute for Textile Technology (RFTITT), [...]
item.content:encoded:
The EASTRIP SDTVET/World Bank Mission has commenced its closing implementation support mission and National Steering Committee (NSC) meetings with a site visit to Kisumu National Polytechnic, home to the KSh 1.2 billion World Bank-funded East Africa Skills for Transformation and Regional Integration Project (EASTRIP).

Designated as the Regional Flagship TVET Institute for Textile Technology (RFTITT), the institution is strengthening specialised skills development to support the textile industry and regional integration.

The mission, comprising World Bank officials, NSC members, the National Project Coordinating Unit and representatives of the five Regional Flagship TVET Institutes, toured the textile and ginnery factory, student accommodation, classrooms and workshops to assess project implementation progress.

The team subsequently held a consultative meeting with EASTRIP stakeholders to review implementation progress, address outstanding issues and provide guidance ahead of the project’s scheduled closure on 31 December 2026.

The TVET Authority Ag. Director General Timothy Katiambo also graced the function.

The mission will proceed to Naivasha for tomorrow’s a site visit to KenGen’s Geothermal Training Centre, followed by the Kenya Institute of Highways and Building Technology (KIHBT), the regional flagship institution specialising in highways technology, to assess progress and project implementation.

These engagements underscore the importance of strategic partnerships in strengthening TVET infrastructure, advancing specialised skills development and preparing a skilled workforce to meet Kenya’s and the region’s evolving industry needs.
